root_idea.summary: Directed intention: aiming at, deliberately intending, or choosing a target.
root_idea.development: The supplied root analysis develops from قصد and تعمد toward directing intention at a specified object. It explicitly treats the sea term as separate from this core analogy.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Classical Arabic perfect citation form.
The packet supplies Quran Foundation contextual glosses for يَمّ but no Lane primary or unique Mufradat definition establishing a Quranic form-level sense; contextual English alone is insufficient.

senses.definition: To aim at, intend, or deliberately turn toward a chosen object.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic purification construction, the intended object is clean earth (ṣaʿīd); this is a constructional application of the sense of deliberate aiming or seeking rather than a separate lexical meaning. The same form also denotes directing one's aim toward good things.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The sea; a large body of water.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal lexical item treated separately from the root's core analogy of directed intention.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who obtains whatever he seeks; hence, one toward whom good is directed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A descriptive use for a person, including a poetic application in which good is directed toward him.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who has fallen into the sea and drowned.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported derived descriptive form for a person who meets this fate.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A bird, described as one that breeds in houses.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separate nominal lexical item, not a direct extension of the core meaning of directed intention.

cautions: The Quranic nominal group يَمّ has contextual glosses meaning “the sea” and “the river,” but it is not assigned a numbered Quranic sense because the packet lacks qualifying direct form-level lexical evidence.
Several Lane entries are only pointers to omitted articles, so their referenced Form II and technical constructions are not expanded beyond what the supplied text securely establishes.
unassigned_or_ambiguous_evidence: The eight Quranic occurrences of يَمّ are supported here only by contextual English glosses (“the sea” and “the river”) and by a Maqayis discussion; because Maqayis alone cannot establish a direct Quran-form sense, the QAC nominal group is excluded from the public Quranic forms.
The Form II phrase يَمَّمَ المَرِيضَ والمَيِّتَ in lane:entry:12183 is cross-referenced to an unsupplied article, so its precise lexical construction cannot be assigned confidently.
الفَرِيضَةُ اليَمِّيَّةُ in lane:entry:12185 is recorded only as a cross-reference to المُشَرَّكَةُ; the supplied packet does not define this technical expression.
